bachelor-thesis.title: Bachelor Thesis - Telenor
bachelor-thesis.description: Design and development of a shared, web-based knowledge platform for consistent and efficient technical troubleshooting at Telenor.

problem.title: Problem
problem.text: Telenor identified challenges related to fragmented troubleshooting information across customer self-service and internal support systems. Customers often failed to resolve technical issues independently and contacted support instead, leading to inconsistent guidance, reduced trust, and increased workload for customer service agents.

research.title: Research
research.text: The project combined qualitative and quantitative research methods, including semi-structured interviews with customer service agents, customer surveys, call-monitoring sessions, and competitor analysis. Findings highlighted issues related to information architecture, technical language, and lack of visual guidance during troubleshooting.

keyInsight.title: Key Insight
items: Users struggled to find the right answer quickly
Inconsistent terminology created confusion
Support agents used multiple tools daily

design.title: Design
design.text: Using the Double Diamond framework, the solution was designed through iterative prototyping, user flows, personas, sitemap development, and accessibility-focused design decisions. Particular focus was placed on clear language, consistent information structures, and seamless escalation from self-service to customer support.

development.title: Development
development.text: The platform was implemented as a fullstack web application using Next.js, PostgreSQL, and role-based authentication. Separate customer and agent portals shared a common knowledge base, while CI/CD pipelines, Docker, and accessibility testing ensured maintainability and scalability.

testing.title: Testing
testing.text: The prototype was evaluated through usability testing with both customers and customer service agents. All participants completed their assigned tasks successfully, while findings emphasized the importance of enhanced visual support such as router images, cable illustrations, and indicator light guidance.

result.title: Result
result.text: The final solution introduced a shared knowledge platform with separate customer and agent interfaces, reducing fragmented information and improving consistency in troubleshooting guidance. Usability testing showed that all participants successfully completed their tasks, indicating a clear improvement in user flow and understanding.

study-platform.title: Study Platform
study-platform.description: StudyPlatform is a web-based research system designed to support the creation and execution of multimedia comparison studies. It enables researchers to design structured studies using different types of media such as images, videos, audio, and text, and collect participant responses in a controlled and scalable way.

problem.title: Problem
problem.text: Traditional survey tools such as Google Forms and SurveyMonkey are not designed for research scenarios involving rich media comparisons. They provide limited flexibility for study design, lack support for structured artifact evaluation, and offer weak tools for managing research workflows and participant data.

solution.title: Solution
solution.text: StudyPlatform introduces a centralized environment where researchers can create and manage multiple studies, upload and organize multimedia research artifacts, design flexible question formats and rating scales, distribute studies through shareable participant links, track participation and study progress, and export structured datasets for analysis.

keyInsight.title: Key Insight
items: Create and manage multiple studies from a single dashboard
Upload and organize multimedia research artifacts
Design flexible question formats and rating scales
Distribute studies through shareable participant links
Track participation and study progress in real time
Export structured datasets for analysis

design.title: Design
design.text: Using the Double Diamond framework, the solution was designed through iterative prototyping, user flows, personas, sitemap development, and accessibility-focused design decisions.

result.title: Result
result.text: The final system provides researchers with a more flexible and research-oriented alternative to traditional survey tools, enabling structured comparative studies with richer data inputs and improved workflow management.
impact: Study dashboard with live overview of responses
Participant tracking and anonymized data handling

spanish-poker.title: Spanish Poker Dice
spanish-poker.description: This project was developed as part of a full-stack exam assignment at NTNU, where the goal was to build a complete multiplayer web platform for managing and playing a turn-based dice game.

design.title: Design
design.text: Before implementing features, we created quick lo-fi wireframes and hi-fi mockups to visualize key flows such as the game lobby, matchmaking, game board, tournament overview, user profile, and statistics dashboard.

realTime.title: Real-time System
realTime.text: A major part of the project was implementing real-time interaction using WebSockets. This enabled live updates of game actions, synchronized gameplay across multiple players, hidden game state logic handled on the backend, and immediate UI updates without page reloads.

authentication.title: Authentication & Security
items: JWT access and refresh tokens
Password hashing and salting
Email verification flow with time-limited tokens
Role-based access control

finalResult.title: Final Result
items: Real-time dice gameplay for 2–5 players
Tournament system with progression and ranking
User authentication and profile management
Admin dashboard for platform control
Responsive UI with game, lobby, and profile views

samfundet.title: UI/UX Redesign Samfundet Gjøvik
samfundet.description: Redesigned Samfundet Gjøvik’s website to improve usability, accessibility, and overall visual consistency through UX research, evaluation, and prototyping in Figma.

problem.title: Problem
items: Inconsistent visual design and weak overall identity
Poor accessibility
Confusing structure and navigation
Booking and event flow lacked clarity

research.title: Research
research.text: We conducted multiple UX evaluation methods to identify key issues, including heuristic evaluation, in-person usability testing, design evaluation, and competitor analysis.

keyInsight.title: Key Insight
items: Users struggled to understand site structure
Booking and event flow was unclear
Accessibility issues affected readability and usability
Inconsistent UI elements reduced trust and clarity

moscow.title: MoSCoW
moscow.text: We used the MoSCoW method to prioritize improvements, including WCAG compliance, better content structure, improved contrast, consistent UI components, and improved booking and contact flows.

design.title: Design & Prototyping
design.text: We developed a full redesign in Figma, including wireframes, high-fidelity prototypes, desktop and mobile versions, a consistent design system, and improved UI patterns and accessibility.

improvements.title: What could be improved
items: Adding dark mode for better user comfort
Improving carousel navigation on desktop
Adding quick home navigation
Enhancing calendar and event interaction features
Potential internal employee portal

result.title: Result
items: Improved UX structure
Better accessibility
More consistent UI system
Clearer user flows for booking and events

helserett.title: HelseRett.no
helserett.description: A UX and interaction design project focused on making health information easier, safer, and more accessible for older users. I explored user needs and challenges related to digital healthcare services and used these insights to develop and test a user-friendly solution.
helserett.projectGoal: The goal was to create a digital healthcare service that makes it easier for older users to find, understand, and access relevant health information.
helserett.targetAudience: Older users with varying levels of digital literacy who need clear, simple, and accessible health information.
process: Analysis of user challenges and needs
helserett.keyLearnings: The project gave me a deeper understanding of the importance of exploring real user needs before starting the design process. Insights from users influenced how information was structured, how navigation was designed, and how the solution could be made more accessible and easier to use.
helserett.outcome: The result was a user-centered prototype focused on clear information, simple navigation, accessibility, and a more intuitive experience for older users.
